mediaComposer.purpose: Bounded installed Media Composer own MXF descriptor Bit Depth import/publication audit, separating audio quantization bits, picture component width, RGBA roles/widths, total pixel size and numeric representation.
mediaComposer.method: Read-only static arm64 named disassembly; previously connected ordinary MXF scanner to own physical SourceMob EssenceDescriptor/CreateDescriptor/ConvertDescriptorFromAAF; typed toolkit vtables and numeric/string constants checked. No app/private API/media execution.

findings.topic: Audio quantization bits are imported independently of frequency and coding
findings.evidence: The own descriptor sound importer obtains unsigned 32-bit QuantizationBits through its typed interface, then calls the descriptor BitsPerSample setter. It separately imports AudioSamplingRate and sound essence coding. QuantizationBits is an audio bit count, not the picture special-code enumeration or a combined width multiplied by channels. The engine setter stores an unsigned halfword at this+0x27e and a nonzero-known flag at +0x280; that native internal 16-bit limit is not the wire type and need not be copied into Bella.

findings.topic: Audio metadata publishes quantization bits separately
findings.evidence: The audio publisher obtains BitsPerSample from the same descriptor and emits QuantizationBits as numeric metadata. PCM GetSampleFormat separately branches on internal AudioCodingFormat and, for some cases, width/known flags. A numeric 32-bit audio width does not alone establish integer versus floating-point representation. The native coding converter and sample-format branch are recorded as context; this audit does not claim a complete codec dictionary or universal GUI label.

findings.topic: Picture CDCI imports and publishes raw component width
findings.evidence: The own CDCI descriptor importer reads ComponentWidth through its typed toolkit interface and retains the raw 32-bit component code. Native AAF interface spelling is ComponentWidth; corresponding MXF metadata publication is ComponentDepth. This describes one picture component, not packed bits per pixel, bitrate, sampled raster size or a master property. The toolkit getter uses an int output; this alone does not redefine the MXF wire property declared type. MPEG-family inheritance is established in the preceding descriptor audits, not a newly invented per-codec field guess.

findings.topic: Alpha depth is a separate picture fact
findings.evidence: Native CDCI metadata publishes AlphaSampleDepth independently from ComponentDepth. Do not let an alpha precision override the colour component width. RGBA component role A is likewise a distinct recorded role; a physical alpha-only RGBA file can describe its own alpha precision without proving RGB precision of a separate colour file. The complete native UI policy for mixed/alpha-only layouts is not traced.

findings.topic: RGBA typed layout becomes separate native arrays, not MDB wire arrays
findings.evidence: The own typed RGBA importer obtains component records and separates component codes from their paired size bytes into native layout/structure arrays. Its aligned toolkit records stride eight bytes with the size at offset four; that is an in-memory ABI layout after typed decoding, not raw MXF wire layout. Native aafGetLayoutArray explicitly handles roles including R/G/B/A, F, P, null and further code values, and reports unsupported codes. The MDB parallel arrays and raw MXF interleaved layout must not be conflated.

findings.topic: Toolkit supports null and ASCII-zero unused RGBA components; counting is not a simple terminator walk
anchors: impl vtable offsets0x380/0x388 resolve to count/get functions
findings.evidence: The toolkit count method examines all eight aligned component code fields, counting values other than numeric0 and ASCII zero(0x30). It does not stop at the first null and does not validate trailing widths in this method. GetPixelLayout copies the first requested count records, rather than compacting all meaningful records. SetPixelLayout explicitly fills unused records with component code0x30 and width0. Thus native itself supports ASCII-zero/zero padding; rejecting every nonzero byte after a null component can lose compatible data.

specificExample.interpretation: A8, then null/0, then six ASCII-zero/0 pairs. Applying the statically traced code-count rule gives1 and the selected engine receives first A8 only. This is a manual inference from supplied bytes plus native instructions, not executed MC or an independently re-read media sample.

findings.bellaBoundary: Bella stopping at a valid0/0 terminator within a complete bounded16-byte PixelLayout is a separate simpler compatibility design, not an identical copy of the toolkit all-eight counting method. Known ASCII-zero/0 unused padding is directly corroborated by the native setter. Arbitrary meaningful data, invalid widths or holes elsewhere are not universally validated or safely recovered by this native trace.

findings.topic: Native RGBA publisher rebuilds interleaved component-size bytes
findings.evidence: The publisher takes the separate native code and size arrays, builds alternating one-byte code and one-byte size values, and enforces a 16-byte metadata layout. This independently connects representation publication, but does not make native in-memory structs identical to the wire or establish that a per-component depth column should sum every component.

findings.topic: Special picture codes and codec context must remain qualified
findings.evidence: The existing verified native generic pixel-width helper maps picture component codes 253,254,255 to storage widths16,32,64 before pixel/subsampling arithmetic; a separate component-format getter first consults dynamic codec context. Native RGBA calculation also uses component-format lookup and repair/default paths. Neither helper is a universal Bit Depth GUI decoder. The separately verified Avid DNxUncompressed RDD50 context can give raw254 a16-bit S2.14 meaning rather than generic32-bit float, so preserve complete known coding UL plus raw code where required. Never emit 254-bit from the sentinel, apply picture sentinels to audio QuantizationBits, infer float from audio32 alone, or silently copy native RGB8 repair defaults.

findings.topic: Failure behavior does not define a universal native availability contract
anchors: CDCI GetComponentWidth result not checked immediately after 0x342d50
RGBA CalcPixelWidthComponentFormat fallback/repair paths in prior receipt
findings.evidence: The native audio getter failure enters assertion/debug machinery and can continue with initialized output; selected CDCI and RGBA getter calls have their own result/default handling rather than one clean blank policy. Zero or an unrecognized code is not thereby a valid display depth. Bella missing/damaged/unsupported-to-unavailable rules are explicit design decisions; no uniform malformed guarantee or native blank GUI parity is proved.

sourceFindings.detail: Current essence-qualified physical SourcePackage owns its descriptor. Audio depth uses GenericSoundEssenceDescriptor.QuantizationBits; CDCI/MPEG uses inherited CDCIEssenceDescriptor.ComponentDepth; both are complete unsigned big-endian32 properties. RGBA uses16-byte PixelLayout, eight fixed interleaved one-byte Code/Depth pairs. Legacy MDB parallel PixelLayout/PixelStructure arrays are a different representation. No UTF8/MacRoman decoding or summed bits-per-pixel is needed for per-component depth.

numericFormat emits strings early. With exact standard DNxUncompressed coding060e2b340401010d0401020203070100,253=>16-bit Half float,254=>32-bit Float,8/10/12/16=>same-width Integer,other codes unavailable. Exact fixed variant...03070200 accepts254=>16-bit S2.14,10=>16-bit10.6,12=>16-bit12.4;other codes unavailable. These known-label branches precede generic handling. Otherwise generic picture253/254/255=>16-half/32-float/64-float,ordinary1..32=>same-width Integer; audio1..64=>same-width depth without inferring representation merely from QuantizationBits. Audio253/254/255 are not picture float enumerations.

Current projector records raw ComponentDepth/QuantizationBits observation then derived BitDepth/SampleFormat strings. A complete Wave/AES3 descriptor with absent sound coding establishes PCM Integer through a separate codec branch. A missing depth does not turn into24-bit or a codec-advertised maximum. CDCIAlphaSampleDepth separately records alpha presence for nonnegative decoded values; it is not substituted for the colour depth. RGBA A/a marks alpha presence separately, including alpha-only media. Necessary representation affects existing Compression naming but no new visible format/alpha column is required.

sourceFindings.topic: RGBA current validation and mixed widths
sourceFindings.detail: Current RGBA loop requires eight decoded pairs, recognized codes, positive depth for each nonzero code and zero depth for zero code. Code0 starts termination; any later nonzero code/depth rejects the whole derived RGBA projection. F is ignored for colour/alpha precision. Palette P rejects generic depth projection rather than reporting index width. Interpretable common widths collapse to one N-bit string; mixed interpreted widths retain per-component strings rather than blank. That is current behavior, not Bella adopting mixed strings.

A recognized positive-depth component increments activeComponents, but an unsupported numericFormat result is simply omitted from depth/format lists; other interpreted components can still produce a derived label. Thus structural completeness alone does not guarantee every meaningful component was interpreted. This is a static potential partial-depth claim, not an observed erroneous result in the sampledfiles. Bella proposed commonwidth handling should require every relevant component usable before agreement.

unique rejects unreadable/invalid or conflicting repeated values. Bad bounds/types and unusable ownership cannot become chosen depth. Unsupported scalar codes retain raw ComponentDepth but no interpreted BitDepth; coverage distinguishes unsupported interpretation from actual absence. Multiple owned descriptor child observations may conflict at equal priority; current resolver blanks incompatible selected labels. Retain physical row and independently valid fields.

Current numericFormat produces depth and representation QStrings in the projector; evidence retains raw coded numeric facts and format context alongside derived strings. Adapter stores selected BitDepth QString; numeric variants are converted to N-bit there. MediaFile row keeps QString bitDepth. Table/CSV reuse it. Sort extracts number only from a simple positive N-bit label, then text tiebreak; mixed component strings sort in other-label group. Bella already chose numericdepth+neededformat and late labels; copying current value graphs/string storage is unnecessary.

proposal.specialCodes: Carry verified standard picture253/254/255 half/32float/64float and full-coding-qualified DNxUncompressed rules into small helpers. Standard254→32float; exact fixed variant254→16S2.14. Preserve raw code and needed representation/coding ID. Do not print raw254-bit or infer from a codec headline/maximum. Existing unresolved10.6/12.4 generic labels stay separate.
proposal.rgbaPadding: Require interpretable meaningful prefix; numeric00/00 or nativeASCII30/00 starts end/padding and all remaining pairs must be these known forms. Reject nonpadding tails and preserve16bytebound. Do not reproduce native non-prefix count/copy quirks.
proposal.rgbaNumericPolicy: Every meaningful non-fill component must be supported/interpreted. Common interpreted width gives one numeric depth, including alpha-only files. No sum/first-component/partial-result shortcut. Mixed widths, palette/unsupported component meanings or unverified LSB merges supply no single depth; retain only needed compact layout/context.
proposal.missingDamaged: Unavailable selected source supplies no MXF Bit Depth; keep physical file and independently usable facts. No guessed default, codec capability substitution or consistency graph.
proposal.storageAndDisplay: One interpreted numeric depth with necessary source/rawcode/layout/representation/availability; labels generated later and numeric sorting. No new visible alpha/sample-format column or permanent depth label as source truth.
